methodology.Fees: All transaction (gas) fees paid by users on the NEAR blockchain, fetched from Allium.
methodology.Revenue: 70% of every gas fee is permanently burned, reducing NEAR supply. The other 30% is paid to contract developers, so only 70% is protocol revenue.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Burned gas fees (70%) accrue to all NEAR holders through reduced circulating supply.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The remaining 30% of each gas fee is rebated to the developer of the smart contract being called.

methodology.Fees: Gross fees charged on NEAR Intents swaps - the protocol fee plus the affiliate (distribution) fee each frontend collects, summed across all integrators.
methodology.Revenue: NEAR's net captured revenue, measured as NEAR/wNEAR swept into its revenue wallets (reconciles with revenue.near.org and the on-chain buyback). Split by destination wallet into front-end affiliate revenue and Other. Transfers between those wallets are excluded.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Captured revenue held by the treasury before the 2026-02-23 buyback program.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Since 2026-02-23, NEAR's captured Intents revenue is used to buy back $NEAR on the open market (not burned), returning value to holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Gross fees minus NEAR's captured revenue - the affiliate fees kept by solvers and third-party distribution channels (e.g. SwapKit).

tests.claim: More money is swapping through NEAR Intents than a year ago
tests.name: Intents demand is compounding
tests.metric: Intents volume, trailing 90d vs same 90d one year earlier

tests.claim: NEAR is capturing more of that flow as revenue
tests.name: Captured Intents revenue is rising
tests.metric: NEAR holders revenue (buyback-directed), trailing 90d vs prior 90d

tests.claim: People still use the NEAR base layer
tests.name: Base-layer usage is retained
tests.metric: Avg daily active accounts, trailing 90d vs same 90d one year earlier

tests.claim: Each remaining user pays more in fees
tests.name: Remaining activity is economically denser
tests.metric: Gas fees per active account, trailing 90d vs one year earlier

tests.claim: Buybacks and burn outweigh new token issuance
tests.name: Holder value offsets dilution
tests.metric: (Annualised Intents holders revenue + gas burn) / annual gross issuance value

tests.claim: Intents activity moves before the NEAR price
tests.name: Intents volume leads NEAR price
tests.metric: Max weekly lead correlation (1–4w) vs Bonferroni critical r
tests.rule: pass if best leading r > critical r (0.2513) over 99 weeks · otherwise fail

leadLag.method: Pearson correlation of week-over-week log changes; positive lag = Intents volume leads NEAR price. Complete ISO weeks only. Bonferroni-adjusted critical |r| for 4 leading lags (alpha 0.05).

limitations: NearBlocks 'active_accounts' counts distinct signer accounts, not humans; part of the year-over-year decline reflects the end of high-volume incentive and bot campaigns, which this data cannot separate from organic churn.

DefiLlama Intents volume counts swap input notional; it is not revenue. Holders revenue is NEAR's captured share swept to revenue wallets and, since 2026-02-23, used for open-market buybacks (DefiLlama methodology). Buybacks are treated as holder value in USD, not as burned supply.
Issuance is measured from the change in total supply plus burned NEAR; staking rewards are a transfer to stakers, so non-staked holders bear the dilution measured here.
NearBlocks circulating supply appears static; total supply is used for all supply calculations.

The lead/lag test is correlational over a short history and says nothing about causality. Its lags, frequency and critical value were set after the 2026-11-12 snapshot had been seen and are frozen since tag thresholds-v1; changing them would invalidate it.
Only keyless public aggregators are used here. The BigQuery pipeline (scripts/rebuild.py) gives contract-level detail from raw chain data and needs Google Cloud credentials.
